body.v: We have updated the terms of your e-banking agreement. Please sign in to accept them by the end of the week.
Without acceptance your access may be limited.

hotspots.explain: swissa1pbank.example has the digit 1 in place of the letter l. It is not swissalpbank.example.
"By the end of the week" gives you a deadline you did not choose.
"Access may be limited" is a threat to make you act.
The sign-in page is on the lookalike domain and would copy your login.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone using the bank's name. The address has a digit 1 where the letter l belongs: swissa1pbank.example is not swissalpbank.example. Your eyes can miss a one-letter swap, but a password manager never does.
choices: SwissAlpBank, because it knows your name

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: Fear and hurry: you could lose access if you do not act by the end of the week.
choices: Fear of losing access, with a deadline

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Sign in to 'accept' new terms, which would give your login to the sender.

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Use your password manager's saved SwissAlpBank login. It checks the exact web address and will not fill in on a lookalike site: if it stays quiet, that is your warning. Or open the bank's app yourself.
choices: Click the link and check that the page looks right
Open the saved login in your password manager, or the app yourself
Type your password by hand if the manager does not fill it in

actions.label: Open the bank from your password manager's saved login, or the app
actions.consequence: Nothing to accept. If you had clicked the email, the manager would not have filled anything in.

actions.label: Click the link and type your password
actions.consequence: The page looks right, but your login goes straight to the scammer.

actions.label: The password manager does not fill in, so type the password by hand
actions.consequence: The manager stayed quiet because the address was wrong. You overrode your best warning.

actions.label: Report it as phishing and delete it
actions.consequence: Good call. You gave nothing away.

attacker_reveal: A single digit in place of a letter... Your eyes skip it, but a password manager compares every character. When it refuses to fill in, believe it.
